{{Trail|Items}}
'''Food''' items can be eaten to [[Skyrim:Restore Health|restore]] your [[Skyrim:Health|health]] or [[Skyrim:Stamina|stamina]], and some provide additional benefits to magicka, archery, block, barter, carry weight, cure disease, poison/fire/frost resistance, waterbreathing, or warmth. 

Raw food provides only trivial benefits, but it can be [[Skyrim:Cooking|cooked]] into 58 food items, 2 poisoned apples, and 17 hot soups, or [[Skyrim:Baking|baked]] into 15 food items, to increase the benefits. Food is cheaper and more widely available than potions, and creating cooked food does not involve the [[Skyrim:Alchemy|Alchemy]] skill. However, even cooked food typically provides weaker effects than potions do. Nonetheless, a small number of dishes provide quite long-lasting effects, with several of the soups, stews, and bisques like [[#Beef Stew|Beef Stew]] lasting longer than all stamina potions, and [[#Elsweyr Fondue|Elsweyr Fondue]] is actually more powerful than a number of magicka potions.

Stamina regeneration food such as vegetable soup is rather useful for melee based characters; the stamina regeneration each second allows you to use power attacks continuously until the effect wears off. Alcoholic beverages like ale, mead, and wine typically provide an immediate boost to stamina but reduced stamina regeneration for a period of time.

Most food items can be sold to any innkeeper or food vendor, as well as to general goods merchants (exceptions are noted in the following tables). A limited number of food items are categorized as raw food, and these items can also be sold to apothecary merchants. In addition, innkeepers and food vendors will have a selection of food items available for purchase.

With the addition of [[Skyrim:Survival Mode|Survival Mode]] food is also used to replenish [[Skyrim:Hunger|Hunger]]. Different foods have different weights of replenishment lowering the Hunger meter by set amounts. Very small replenishes 2, small replenishes 18, medium replenishes 220, and large replenishes 380.

Foods added by [[Skyrim:Dawnguard|Dawnguard]], [[Skyrim:Dragonborn|Dragonborn]], [[Skyrim:Hearthfire|Hearthfire]], and [[Skyrim:Creation Club|Creation Club]] are annotated with "DG", "DB", "HF", and "CC" superscripts, respectively. 

==Regular Food==
This section includes all food items that cannot be created by the player by [[Skyrim:Baking|baking]] or [[Skyrim:Cooking|cooking]], although most of these items can be used as ingredients in baking and cooking recipes. Several of these items are also classified by merchants as being raw food; they can be sold to apothecary merchants and innkeepers.

===Raw Meat===
{{Showhide/Start|expanded=on}}
Raw meat can generally be obtained from the bodies of dead [[Skyrim:Animals|animals]]. In the case of small game (e.g., rabbits and pheasants), already-caught animals can also be found hanging in homes and inns, and can be harvested to obtain the meat. Similarly, salmon can also be found hanging from racks near rivers. A variety of fish can be caught by hand or by using a [[Skyrim:Fishing Items#Weapons|rod]] with the [[Skyrim:Fishing (activity)|Fishing]] [[Skyrim:Fishing|Creation]]. Certain barrels are internally identified as meat barrels and will always contain raw meat, as well as [[Skyrim:Salt Pile|salt pile]]s and other ingredients.

Three stall merchants, [[Skyrim:Hogni Red-Arm|Hogni Red-Arm]] in [[Skyrim:Markarth|Markarth]], [[Skyrim:Anoriath|Anoriath]] in [[Skyrim:Whiterun|Whiterun]] and [[Skyrim:Marise Aravel|Marise Aravel]] in [[Skyrim:Riften|Riften]], specialize in raw meat. In addition, some varieties of meat can be bought from [[Skyrim:Hunter|hunter]]s encountered in the wilderness.

Nearly all raw meat can be cooked by simply combining it with salt. A few meats (beef, chicken, clams, crab, horker, venison) can also be made into more elaborate dishes or stews by combining them with vegetables as well as salt.

* One sack of flour is one of five items needed to bake a [[Skyrim:Juniper_Berry_Crostata|juniper berry crostata]]{{HF}}.
* One sack of flour is one of five items needed to bake a [[Skyrim:Lavender_Dumpling|lavender dumpling]]{{HF}}.
* One sack of flour is one of five items needed to bake [[Skyrim:Potato_Bread|potato bread]]{{HF}}.
* One sack of flour is one of four items needed to bake a [[Skyrim:Snowberry_Crostata|snowberry crostata]]{{HF}}.
* One sack of flour is one of five items needed to bake a [[Skyrim:Sweet Roll|sweet roll]].
|}

{{Mod Note|Survival Mode}}

==={{Anchor|Hot Soups|Hot SoupsCC}}{{CC|Survival Mode}}===
{{Showhide/Start|expanded=1}}
These 17 soup recipes are made at the standard cooking locations but are only available to be crafted if Survival Mode is enabled as part of the [[Skyrim:Survival Mode|Survival Mode]] [[Skyrim:Creation Club|Creation]]. Their primary use is to counteract the [[Skyrim:Cold|cold]], but they also act as [[Skyrim:Hunger|hunger]] reducers.

There are no guaranteed locations for any of the hot soups.

==Beverages==
{{Showhide/Start|expanded=1}}
Consuming alcoholic beverages like meads, wines, and brandies typically provide an immediate boost to stamina, along with reduced stamina regeneration, for a period of time.

Several other alcoholic beverages are classified as [[Skyrim:Potions|potions]] instead of food, meaning they are displayed in your inventory under potions: 
* [[Skyrim:Argonian Ale|Argonian Ale]]
* [[Skyrim:Balmora Blue|Balmora Blue]] wine
* [[Skyrim:Cliff Racer|Cliff Racer]] wine
* [[Skyrim:Cyrodilic Brandy|Cyrodilic Brandy]]
* [[Skyrim:Skooma|Skooma]], including [[Skyrim:Double-Distilled Skooma|Double-Distilled Skooma]] and [[Skyrim:Kordir's Skooma|Kordir's Skooma]]
* [[Skyrim:Stros M'Kai Rum|Stros M'Kai Rum]]
* [[Skyrim:Velvet LeChance|Velvet LeChance]] wine
* [[Skyrim:White-Gold Tower|White-Gold Tower]] wine
Many of these other beverages do not have the negative reduced stamina regeneration side effect.

==Notes==
*During [[Skyrim:A Night To Remember|A Night To Remember]], only the Alto Wine variant with the basket on the bottom counts as a quest item; the one that lacks it doesn't. Likewise, regular wine, Spiced Wine, and empty wine bottles also do not count.
*Your inventory says that cabbages, eidar cheese wedges, goat cheese wedges, and Sadri's Sujamma weigh 0.3 instead of 0.25. It is unknown if this is normal or a bug.
*Version 2.0.9 of the [[Skyrim Mod:Unofficial Skyrim Patch|Unofficial Skyrim Patch]] makes it possible to sell a good majority of the original player-cooked foods to food and drink vendors, as well as Firebrand Wine and Colovian Brandy.
**Version 2.0.9 of the [[Skyrim Mod:Unofficial Dragonborn Patch|Unofficial Dragonborn Patch]] also makes it possible to sell Horker and Ash Yam Stew to food and drink vendors, as well as some of the food exclusively found on [[Skyrim:Solstheim|Solstheim]], such as Boar Meat.
***Version 1.0.1 of the [[Skyrim Mod:Unofficial Hearthfire Patch|Unofficial Hearthfire Patch]] makes it possible to sell Potato Soup and Clam Chowder to food and drink vendors.

==Bugs==
{{Bug|Vegetable Soup and Venison Stew may not restore health properly.|OSSEP|1.5.73}}
{{Bug|Seared Slaughterfish and Charred Skeever Meat may restore less Hunger than intended.|OSSEP|1.6}}
{{Bug|Some food and drink items may not make the proper sounds when picked up, dropped, and/or consumed.|OSSEP|1.6}}
{{Bug|Flin, Mazte, Shein, Sujamma, Sadri's Sujamma, and Emberbrand Wine all lack proper pickup and drop sounds.|USLEEP|3.0.8}}
{{Bug|Boar Meat, Ash Hopper Meat, Ash Hopper Leg, and Cooked Boar Meat all display 0 value due to not having set the no-autocalc flag on them.|USLEEP|3.0.8}}
{{Bug|Horker and Ash Yam Stew doesn't use the same eating sounds used by every other stew object in the game.|USSEP|4.2.5}}
